description:
Sources Sought Notice  

 Spectrum Engineering Technical Support Services for the Navy and Marine Corps Spectrum Center (NMSC) 

  
This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is in anticipation of a potential future procurement under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code  541330, Engineering Services . Subject to FAR 15.101, entitled  Early Exchanges with Industry , this announcement constitutes an SSN for written information only. This is not a solicitation announcement for proposals, and no contract will be awarded from this announcement. This SSN is not to be construed in any way as a commitment by the U.S. Government, nor will the U.S. Government pay for the information submitted in response. 

 Failure to respond to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future Request for Proposal (RFP) or Request for Quotation (RFQ), should one be issued. In the event a solicitation is released in the future, it will be posted to the Governmentwide Point of Entry at SAM.gov. Potential offerors/quoters are responsible for monitoring the site for updates and additional information regarding this requirement. 

  1. Description  

 The Naval Supply Systems Command (NAVSUP) Fleet Logistics Center (FLC) Norfolk Contracting Department is seeking information from interested sources capable of providing Spectrum Engineering and Technical Support Services in support of the Navy and Marine Corps Spectrum Center (NMSC). 

 The requirement includes specialized engineering, analytical, software development and sustainment, and administrative support associated with electromagnetic spectrum management, spectrum certification, electromagnetic compatibility, and national security missions. 

 The specific acquisition strategy has not yet been finalized. Interested parties are encouraged to review the attached draft Performance Work Statement (PWS), which outlines the types of tasks the contractor would be required to perform. 

  2. Requirements  

 The Government is conducting market research to determine the availability and capabilities of potential sources, including small businesses, to perform the requirements described in the attached draft PWS. 

 The anticipated services include, but are not limited to: 

 
	 Spectrum engineering, certification, and electromagnetic compatibility analysis. 
	 Satellite spectrum engineering and coordination. 
	 Engineering support for commercial broadband installations and spectrum-sharing initiatives. 
	 Joint Tactical Information Distribution System (JTIDS), Multifunctional Information Distribution System (MIDS), and Joint Tactical Radio System (JTRS) engineering and coordination. 
	 Electromagnetic Compatibility Features (EMCF) certification and validation. 
	 Link 16 Pulse Deconfliction Server (LPDS) administration, software development, maintenance, sustainment, and cybersecurity support. 
	 Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) engineering, research, development, test, and evaluation support. 
	 Spectrum supportability risk assessments, acquisition program support, and national spectrum policy analysis. 
	 Specialized administrative and technical coordination support. 
 

 The Government has determined that these services qualify as commercial services, as defined in FAR 2.101. If solicited, it is anticipated that this requirement will fall under NAICS codes  541330 , with a small business size standard of  $25.5 million . The anticipated Product/Service Code (PSC) is  R425 – Support: Professional – Engineering/Technical . 

 The draft PWS identifies performance primarily within the National Capital Region, including Government facilities at Fort Meade, Maryland, and contractor-provided locations. The requirement also includes travel to other locations as necessary. 

 Personnel performing the requirement must meet the security clearance requirements specified in the draft PWS, including Secret-level eligibility and adjudication at contract start, with certain positions potentially requiring higher-level clearances. 

 The Government has not yet finalized the acquisition vehicle, contract type, or small business set-aside determination, if any. 

  3. Capability Statements  

 This is a market research tool. The input provided will help the Government ascertain the interest, capability, and capacity of potential contractors. Standard company brochures will not be reviewed. Submission must not exceed five (5) typewritten pages including cover sheet, using no less than a 10-point font size. 

 Responses should be emailed to Dave Vaughn (david.e.vaughn6.civ@us.navy.mil) and Amber Geusic (amber.m.geusic.civ@us.navy.mil) no later than  05:00 PM EST on 02 December 2026 . 

 Again, this is not a request for proposal. Technical questions and inquiries may be submitted along with the response; however, the Government is not obligated to answer any questions submitted regarding this SSN. Please note that the information contained in this SSN is for informational purposes only and is subject to change prior to the issuance of any formal solicitation, if one is issued at all. 

  Cover Sheet/Header : 

 
	 Full business name, address, point of contact, telephone number, and email address. 
	 Contractor and Government Entity (CAGE) Code. 
	 Small Business Category, if any: Small Business, Small Disadvantaged, 8(a), HUBZone, Woman-owned, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, or other category. 
	 All currently held contracting vehicles under which the vendor can provide the required services (ex. GSA, SEWP, SeaPort-NxG). 
 

  Capability Statement : 

 
	 Demonstrate the requisite skills, resources, personnel, and technical capabilities necessary to perform ALL requirements of the draft PWS. Documentation of relevant technical expertise and qualifications must be presented in sufficient detail for the Government to determine the respondent’s ability to perform the requirement.
